title: Seven Hammer Clangs Taught a Baby Fear, Yet Half of Textbooks Got Little Albert Wrong

acts.name: Fearless 9-Month Baseline & Suspended 4-Foot Steel Bar in 1920
sentences: You think babies are born afraid of rats and fur!
Yet seven hammer clangs wired that fear from scratch!
This is the true story of the Little Albert Experiment.
Here is what went wrong in a hospital nursery.
In nineteen nineteen, Watson and Rayner filmed baby Albert.
At nine months, small like a carry-on bag, he feared nothing.
He reached calmly for a rat, rabbit, and cotton.
Behind him hung a four-foot bar, like a baseball bat.
Watson raised a hammer — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: Seven Steel-Bar Pairings & Neutral Wooden Control Blocks
sentences: Two months later, like a summer break, testing began.
Whenever Albert touched the rat, Watson struck the bar.
That loud clang rang behind him and startled him!
Across two sessions, Watson paired rat and clang seven times.
Next, Rayner set the silent white rat down alone.
Albert whimpered and crawled fast across the mattress!
Was he just crying at everything nearby?
No — between tests, he stacked wooden blocks calmly.
Turning a nursery into a fear lab was a total nightmare.

acts.name: Amygdala Alarm Wiring & Day +5 Fur Generalization
sentences: How did seven clangs rewire a baby so fast?
The clang raced to his auditory cortex, your hearing center.
Inside the thalamus, the relay station, sound met touch.
Instead of thinking, his amygdala, your alarm, linked fur with danger.
Five days later, Rayner tested if fear spread.
Albert pulled back from a rabbit and cotton wool!
He even leaned back from a fuzzy coat.
Yet when blocks returned, he played with calm hands.
But here's the twist: did that phobia last forever?

acts.name: Ben Harris's 1979 Textbook Audit & Unreversed Fear Ethics Failure
sentences: In nineteen seventy-nine, Ben Harris checked over a hundred books.
Over half of them invented myths Watson never saw!
Writers added a bear toy and claimed lifelong terror.
What did Watson's nineteen twenty diary really say?
Within thirty days fear faded unless struck again!
Watson knew one month ahead, like a wall calendar, Albert left.
Yet Watson and Rayner never undid his fear.
Albert left uncured — so who finally built a cure?

acts.name: Mary Cover Jones's 1924 'Little Peter' Exposure Cure & 2014 Identity Sleuthing
sentences: In nineteen twenty-four, Mary Cover Jones found the answer.
She helped young Peter, who feared white rabbits.
Jones set a rabbit twelve feet off, like a compact car.
Daily it moved one foot closer, like a ruler, during snacks.
Snacks let his prefrontal cortex, the planner, calm the alarm.
Soon Peter patted the rabbit and launched exposure therapy!
The researchers were left completely stunned.
In twenty fourteen, records suggested Albert lived to eighty-seven.

acts.name: Modern IRB Child Protections & Graduated Exposure in Daily Life
sentences: What does Little Albert mean for your fears today?
His test sparked strict ethics boards protecting children.
One bad shock can wire your amygdala, your alarm, fast.
You might flinch at a clinic smell or sound.
Hiding from safe triggers keeps that alarm loud.
Use Jones's cure — start far back while calm.
Calm steps teach your prefrontal cortex, your planner, safety.
Which proves learned fear fades when calm steps retrain your alarm.
